subject: DPA: residency term glossary & deletion terminology (proposal)
messages:
From: Sarah Lindstrom <sarah.lindstrom@datapartner.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@datacorp.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify residency/retain/delete terms for DPA

Hi Logan,

Thanks for sending the latest DPA draft. Our legal team has a handful of questions that keep recurring across the document: some clauses reference 'retain', others 'store', and there are mixed references to 'onshore processing' vs 'onshore backup'. To move the redline forward we need a short, agreed glossary and concrete behavior for the retention/deletion obligations (esp. backups, snapshots, and logs).

Could you do two small things for us this week?
- Share a concise glossary with one-sentence definitions for the terms above so our counsel can map them to our internal controls.
- Confirm the maximum erase window (request -> verified erase) for customer data and whether that includes backups or requires separate carve-outs.

We'd like to avoid lengthy iterative redlines if we can converge on terminology first. I'm attaching DataCorp's intake checklist for reference.

Best,
Sarah

Attachment: intake_checklist.pdf (external)
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lindstrom <sarah.lindstrom@datapartner.com>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify residency/retain/delete terms for DPA

Sarah — thanks, and good call on getting the glossary locked first. Quick answers up front:
- We treat 'retain' as a policy-level obligation (how long we keep data for the service), 'store' as a physical placement term (where data resides), and 'erase'/'delete' as the logical action that removes customer data from primary storage.
- Backups/snapshots: by default we retain backups for the configured backup TTL; deletion requests trigger a scheduled removal from primary stores immediately and a backup purge process that completes within the backup retention window unless an explicit carve-out is requested.

I've attached a short glossary and a redline with two alternative erase-window proposals: (A) 30 days for backup purge; (B) 90 days with expedited escrow/exception handling. Option A is our standard. Please review and indicate which is acceptable to you.

Proposed attachments: DPA_redline_v3.docx, DPA_residency_glossary.xlsx

- Logan

Hi Sarah — Rachel here (privacy/legal). I'm looping in a few clarifying points so the glossary maps cleanly to obligations we can operationalize:

- 'Retention' = configured policy per customer (system-level TTL + any contractual overrides). We'll surface the effective policy in the Console and record it in audit logs.
- 'Erase' means: (1) mark data for deletion in metadata index; (2) remove from hot/primary storage within 24 hours; (3) flag for backup purge job at next backup cycle. Backups are not instantly destructed unless you pick Option A + a backup-purge SLA.
- 'Onshore processing' vs 'Onshore backup' — we'll explicitly call out both: processing (live inference and logging) vs backup (periodic snapshot/replication). Different controls and different timelines.

Small ask: can you confirm Acme's preferred option (A or B) for backup purge so we can put a concrete timeline into the redline? If you have a regulatory hold requirement we'll need that spelled out as an exception.

Thanks,
Rachel

Thanks Rachel — this is helpful. DataCorp (Acme Fintech legal) has a couple of follow-ups after reviewing the glossary/redline:

- They cannot accept a 30-day backup purge (Option A) for certain datasets tied to AML/customer disputes; their baseline ask is 90 days unless we can commit to an auditable expedited purge for specific datasets.
- They want a short list of dataset categories that will always be exempt from backup purge (e.g., transaction ledgers for regulated accounts) and a process for submitting exemptions.
- Request explicit language that 'onshore backup' implies the backup copy will not be transferred off-region for at least the retention period unless the customer consents or lawful process requires it.

Attached are redline comments (tracked) and a sample exemption form they use. We can do a call Monday if easier.

Sarah

Subject: Re: Clarify residency/retain/delete terms for DPA

Sarah — appreciate the clear asks. To keep momentum, I'd like to propose the following compromise we can operationalize without major infra changes:

1) Default: 30-day backup purge for customer-initiated erasure requests.
2) Exception process: customers may nominate dataset categories for a 90-day backup retention (AML/dispute types). Exemption requests must include regulator citation and business justification and will be subject to approval and audit.
3) We will add explicit 'onshore backup' clause: backups for onshore customers will remain within-region for the retention period unless lawful process requires cross-border transfer.

Marissa, looping you in to confirm the engineering effort and whether we can provide an auditable expedited purge path for named datasets (i.e., a prioritized backup queue + verification logs).

If engineering confirms feasibility, I'll accept the exemption workflow and incorporate the language into the DPA redline and glossary. Call Monday morning works for me if you'd prefer to kick-off live.

- Logan

Thanks Logan — quick engineering note after an initial pass:

- We can implement a prioritized backup purge queue for named datasets. Estimated work: small feature (~3 sprint dev effort plus 1 sprint for test/ops automation) if we scope to policy flags rather than per-object indexing.
- We'll emit verification logs (immutable audit entries) when backup purge jobs run; those logs will be available to customers via the Console (and can be exported for compliance reviews).
- Onshore backup clause: we can guarantee backup storage region residency for the retention period provided the customer selects an onshore deployment option and keys are region-bound. Cross-border transfer requires documented consent or legal compulsion.

I'll draft a short ops/implementation summary we can attach to the DPA as an appendix and will flag any hard blockers if they appear during implementation. Logan/Rachel — if you approve, I'll update the redline with the agreed text and attach the ops appendix.

Marissa
